|firstmade=[[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]<ref name="2 BBY">According to ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', the NR-5 series [[Maintenance droid/Legends|repair droid]] was produced by [[Kalibac Industries]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], whose beginning was dated to [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] by ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''. {{Quote|These droids were designed to compete with Cybot Galactica's WED treadwell [sic] units. They're a bit more expensive, but also more reliable.|[[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]] on NR-5 series repair droids, in the ''[[Smuggler's Handbook/Legends|Smuggler's Handbook]]''|<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide" />}}
The '''NR-5 Series Repair Droid''', also known as the '''NR-5 [[Maintenance droid/Legends|maintenance droid]]''' or '''Imperial maintenance droid''', was a knockoff of [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica's]] [[WED Treadwell repair droid/Legends|WED Treadwell repair droid]] manufactured by [[Kalibac Industries]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Despite heavy accusations of stealing the WED's design, it proved hugely popular with [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] and [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Captain/Legends|captains]] alike and was more reliable, if more expensive, than its competitor, even seeing use in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. However, sales of the NR-5 dropped considerably when [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] introduced its [[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4-series agromech droid]], though the NR-5 generally did a better job than the R4 in
the clean environments of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and many remained in use well into the [[New Jedi Order]] era.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|The manipulator arms are stronger, and their personality matrices don't have short attention spans like the WEDs. The tread base is a bit more narrow, allowing it access to some areas the WED droids can't enter. The visual receptors are mounted on a much longer and more adjustable arm, which give it greater ability to poke around in tight spots to find problems with your ship.|Platt Okeefe compares NR-5s and WEDs, in the ''Smuggler's Handbook''|<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide" />}}
[[File:WEDtreadwell-NEGTD.png|thumb|left|200px|The NR-5 was a knockoff of the WED Treadwell repair droid]]
A general maintenance and repair [[Droid/Legends|droid]] that could handle many [[Starship/Legends|starship]] repair tasks,<ref name="Galladinium's Fantastic Technology">''[[Galladinium's Fantastic Technology]]''</ref> the [[Class five droid/Legends|fifth-degree]] NR-5 Series [[Maintenance droid/Legends|Repair Droid]]<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> was a knockoff of the [[WED Treadwell repair droid/Legends|WED Treadwell repair droid]],<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> the very [[Droid/Legends|droid]] it was designed to compete with<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide" /> and bore a striking resemblance to.<ref name="CSWE" /> Designed by [[Kalibac Industries]] to address most maintenance issues aboard commercial and military vessels, it was small and unobtrusive,<ref name="Perlemian Haul" /> standing only 0.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height and able to fit into most repair bays without modifications.<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> It addition, the NR-5's tread bases was a bit more narrow, allowing it access to some areas that WED droid could not enter<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide" /> and traverse all but the most constricted access ducts with relative ease.<ref name="Perlemian Haul" /> The NR-5's two heavy tracks kept it remarkably stable,<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> its three manipulator arms, stronger than those of a WED,<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide" /> made it handy, and its square head and round body were often seen as cute. The NR-5 was equipped with a telescopic<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> heavy grasper [[Limb/Legends|arm]], fine manipulator arm,<ref name="Perlemian Haul" /> and general purpose appendage,<ref name="CSWE" /> with which it was ambidextrous, as well as three tools mounts,<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> an integrated [[Arc welder/Legends|arc welder]], and built-in [[Tool kit/Legends|repair tools]].<ref name="Perlemian Haul" /> Its sophisticated [[Photoreceptor/Legends|visual sensor system]],<ref name="CSWE" /> with [[Human/Legends|Human]] range, ultraviolet,<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> infrared, and low-light capabilities,<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> were mounted on a much longer and more adjustable arm than a WED, which gave it greater ability to poke around in tight spaces to find problems with ships. The NR-5 was also equipped with a wide-band [[Comlink/Legends|comm receptor]],<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide" /> a [[Diagnostic scanner/Legends|diagnostics package]], and a secondary [[Battery/Legends|battery]]. The only problem with the series was that the droid was not particularly sturdy. Though they worked fine in the clean environment of a starship, NR-5s often did not do to well<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> working outdoors<ref name="CSWE" /> in the harsh conditions<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> of many<ref name="CSWE" /> [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> worlds and needed continual maintenance.<ref name="CSWE" />

Intelligent and skilled enough to carry out a wide variety of tasks, but not so curious as to get itself into trouble,<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> NR-5s' simple [[Personality matrix/Legends|personality matrices]]<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> did not have short attention spans like WEDs.<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide" /> Equipped with a Kalibac Industries<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> [[Mechro-II]] [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brain]],<ref name="CSWE" /> they were famous for their determination, which could be both a boon and a liability. Some NR-5s refused to leave their jobs until they were been completed.<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> In addition, they were not particularly bright or personable<ref name="Perlemian Haul" /> and were also cautious. Their [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulators]] were capable of communicating in both [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] and [[Binary/Legends|Binary]], as well as four unassigned [[Language/Legends|languages]], and could read and write in the former.<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" />

==History==
{{Quote|Be careful when purchasing an NR-5. A small company called "Tredwall" is marketing an NR knockoff that works for about ten hours before completely frying all of its circuits!|[[Kraemr]], on [[Cynabar's Droid Datalog]]|<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" />}}
Produced by Kalibac Industries during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="CSWE" /> the awkward NR-5 was considered the perfect maintenance droid when first introduced<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]<ref name="2 BBY" /> for 2,200 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> new. However, the company was heavily accused of stealing the design of<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica's]] cheaper, if less reliable, WED Treadwell unit<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide" /> when it released the droid to market.<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> Despite the allegations being well founded,<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> KI insisted that the NR-5 was their response to the impact of their chief competitor, [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]],<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> and their competing [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series astromech droid]].<ref name="Galladinium's Fantastic Technology" /> It found popularity among shipboard [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] who needed addition assistance in starship maintenance<ref name="CSWE" /> and individuals who needed additional technical help they could count on.<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> In addition, while the NR-5 lacked [[Astrogation/Legends|astrogation]] and [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] skills, it was also substantially cheaper than an R2 unit, making it a good choice for budget conscious [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Captain/Legends|captains]].<ref name="Galladinium's Fantastic Technology" /> Within a year of its release, a small company of [[Outlaw tech/Legends|outlaw techs]] know as "[[Tredwall]]" stole the droid's design and produced a [[NR knockoff|cheap, faulty imitation]] that worked for about ten [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] before completely frying all its circuits.<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> The NR-5 was virtually ignored throughout the Outer Rim Territories after Industrial Automaton introduced its [[R4 astromech droid/Legends|R4-series agromech droid]],<ref name="CSWE" /> causing sales of the former to drop considerably. Still, in gentle conditions the NR-5 generally did a better job than the R4<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> and was commonly regarded as more effective on [[Planet/Legends|planets]] with milder climates,<ref name="CSWE" /> and many remained in use well into the [[New Jedi Order]] era.<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" />

By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], NR-5 Series Repair Droids were assigned to the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy's]] [[Perlemian Haul]] [[Convoy/Legends|convoy]], including the slightly modified [[Temple-class heavy freighter|''Temple''-class heavy freighter]] [[Freighter M226|M226]], and, though largely simple-minded and harmless, were programmed to raise an alarm in the event they spotted unauthorized individuals in their area of activity. Though they had only simple programmings, they were smart enough to recognize that armed individuals lacking uniforms were out of place, especially if they happened to be crawling around a ship's maintenance ducts. If such an encounter took place, an NR-5 would attempt to escape without making too much of a fuss. If confronted violently, it would defend itself using its heavy grasper arm, as well as its integrated arc welder.<ref name="Perlemian Haul" />

==Behind the scenes==
The NR-5 Series Repair Droid was designed and submitted to [[West End Games]] as the NR-5 maintenance droid by [[Greg Dove]] as part of "[[The Fantastic Technology Contest]]," a contest sponsored by the [[Wikipedia:RPGA|Role Playing Game Association Network]], placing 17th out of about 75 entries. As a result, it was included in ''[[Galladinium's Fantastic Technology]]'', a [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] supplement written by [[Rick D. Stuart]] for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''<ref name="Galladinium's Fantastic Technology" /> and released on [[June 1]], [[1995]],<ref name="Fantastic Technology">{{CargoBay|url=item-detail/7761|text=Fantastic Technology}}</ref> where it was depicted in an illustration by [[Christina Wald]].<ref name="Galladinium's Fantastic Technology" /><ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology" /> The NR-5 first appeared in the eighteenth installment of ''[[Star Wars Missions]]'', ''[[Star Wars Missions 18: Rogue Squadron to the Rescue]]'', written by [[Ryder Windham]]<ref name="Star Wars Missions 18">''[[Star Wars Missions 18: Rogue Squadron to the Rescue]]''</ref> and released on [[February 1]], [[1999]].<ref name="Rogue Squadron to the Rescue">{{CargoBay|url=item-detail/802|text=Rogue Squadron to the Rescue}}</ref> It was first identified as the NR-5 Series Repair Droid in ''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]'', a sourcebook written by [[Jeff Grubb]] and [[Owen K.C. Stephens]] for the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''<ref name="Arms & Equipment Guide" /> and released on [[October 1]], [[2002]].<ref name="Arms and Equipment Guide">{{CargoBay|url=item-detail/7254|text=Arms and Equipment Guide}}</ref>
